name: ISS sleep study
description: Average sleep during ISS missions was 6.09 hours per night, well under the 8.5 hours NASA schedules (Barger et al., 2014).
source: Barger LK, Flynn-Evans EE, Kubey A, Walsh L, Ronda JM, Wang W, Wright KP, Czeisler CA. The Lancet Neurology, published 8 Aug 2014.

name: Shuttle sleep study
description: Average sleep during Space Shuttle missions was 5.96 hours per night (Barger et al., 2014).
source: Barger LK, Flynn-Evans EE, Kubey A, Walsh L, Ronda JM, Wang W, Wright KP, Czeisler CA. The Lancet Neurology, published 8 Aug 2014.

name: ISS core temperature study
description: Resting core body temperature rose by about 1.01 °C during six-month ISS stays; the maximum during exercise rose by about 1.39 °C (Stahn et al., 2017).
source: Stahn AC, Werner A, Opatz O, et al. Scientific Reports 7:16180 (2017).

name: ISS blood pressure study
description: 24-hour average blood pressure was lower in space (systolic −8, diastolic −9 mmHg) while cardiac output rose by 41% (Norsk et al., 2015).
source: Norsk P, Asmar A, Damgaard M, Christensen NJ. The Journal of Physiology 593(3):573–584 (2015).

name: ISS muscle study
description: After six months on the ISS, calf muscle volume fell by 13% and peak calf power by 32% despite daily exercise (Trappe et al., 2009).
source: Trappe S, Costill D, Gallagher P, et al. Journal of Applied Physiology 106(4):1159–1168 (2009).
